plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the operation of the BUILD-MAX-HEAP procedure on a 10-element input array A = ⟨4, 1, 3, 2, 16, 9, 10, 14, 8, 7⟩ across six panels (a)–(f). At the top of the figure, the input array A is displayed as a horizontal row of ten labeled cells. Each panel shows the heap as a rooted binary tree in which every node is labeled with its array index (small numeral outside the circle) and its current key value (numeral inside the circle); light gray nodes are unmodified and the single dark gray node labeled i marks the root of the subtree currently being processed by MAX-HEAPIFY. Panel (a) shows the initial tree before any heapification, with i = 5 (value 16) — the first call to MAX-HEAPIFY starting from index ⌊n/2⌋ = 5. Panel (b) shows the state with i = 4 (value 2), after MAX-HEAPIFY has been applied at index 5. Panel (c) shows i = 3 (value 3), with the subtree at index 4 already corrected to place 14 above 2 and 8. Panel (d) shows i = 2 (value 1). Panel (e) shows i = 1 (value 4), the final call, where the root must be sifted down. Panel (f) shows the completed max-heap with root 16, in which no dark node appears and every parent holds a value greater than or equal to its children. This figure illustrates how BUILD-MAX-HEAP constructs a max-heap in place by calling MAX-HEAPIFY on each internal node from index ⌊n/2⌋ down to index 1.

interactionPlan.concept: BUILD-MAX-HEAP turns an arbitrary array into a max-heap in place by calling MAX-HEAPIFY on every internal node from index floor(n/2) down to 1, relying on the fact that each node's two subtrees are already valid heaps when it is processed.
elements: horizontal array bar A of 10 cells, initial values 4,1,3,2,16,9,10,14,8,7, each cell labeled with its 1-based index
rooted binary tree of 10 circular nodes laid out in heap order (root index 1 at top, children 2i and 2i+1 below)
each node shows its array index as a small numeral outside the circle and its current key value inside the circle
light-gray fill for unmodified nodes; dark-gray fill plus an italic 'i' label for the node currently being heapified
comparison arrows from the current node i to its left and right children during a MAX-HEAPIFY step
edges connecting each parent to its children
caption indicating the current phase (e.g. 'MAX-HEAPIFY at i = k' or 'final max-heap')

interactions.label: Implement MAX-HEAPIFY

api.does: returns the array index 2*i of i's left child
returns the array index 2*i+1 of i's right child
reads the key currently stored at index i (read-only)
exchanges the keys at indices i and j — the ONLY way to mutate the array/tree
attach a short text annotation to node i for the learner's own commentary (no state change)

interactions.frame: the whole 10-node tree plus the array bar, with the current node i shaded dark gray and arrows drawn to the two child indices the comparison just touched; one recorded step per value()/swap() call
interactions.success_check: after the bottom-up run, every parent index p satisfies value(p) >= value(2p) and value(p) >= value(2p+1) wherever those children exist (the max-heap property holds for the whole tree)
interactions.teaches: MAX-HEAPIFY must keep sifting the displaced value downward (recursion or loop) until it rests above both of its children — a single swap is not enough, and the bottom-up call order is what lets each call assume its subtrees are already heaps

interactions.label: Run BUILD-MAX-HEAP
interactions.teaches: Pressing run drives the learner's maxHeapify across i = 5,4,3,2,1 in that exact bottom-up order, replaying each sift-down frame by frame so the learner sees why processing leaves-to-root is mandatory

demo_steps.title: The starting array as a tree
demo_steps.narration: The 10-element array is drawn as a complete binary tree in heap order; nothing is a heap yet. BUILD-MAX-HEAP will call your maxHeapify starting at the last internal node, index floor(10/2) = 5, and work upward to the root.

demo_steps.title: Run the correct MAX-HEAPIFY bottom-up
demo_steps.narration: With the correct recursive implementation, pressing run shades each i in dark gray, draws comparison arrows to its children, and swaps values downward until every subtree is a heap — ending in the max-heap with 16 at the root (panel f).

demo_steps.title: Watch a near-miss diverge
demo_steps.narration: Replace the body with the buggy version that swaps once but never recurses. Re-run: the value pushed down at the root is never re-checked against its new children, so the final tree violates the max-heap property — the replay shows exactly where and why it breaks.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: BUILD-MAX-HEAP is correct precisely because it heapifies from floor(n/2) down to 1: when MAX-HEAPIFY runs at node i, both of i's subtrees are already max-heaps, so a single downward sift of i's key is all that is needed to make the subtree rooted at i a heap.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Top: a single horizontal array bar of 10 light-gray cells labeled A with 1-based indices above and the live key values inside, updating in sync with the tree. Below: one complete binary tree (not six static panels) with the root at top center and four levels; each node is a circle with the index as a small numeral just outside the top of the circle and the key value centered inside. Unmodified nodes light gray; the node currently being heapified filled dark gray with an italic 'i' beside it; thin directed arrows from that node to its left and right children appear during each comparison. Edges are simple straight lines. As the run progresses the tree morphs through the configurations of CLRS panels (a)-(f), finishing with 16 at the root, 14 and 10 at level two, and the max-heap property holding everywhere. Keep node positions fixed (heap layout) so only the values and the dark-gray highlight move, making the sift-down visually obvious.

discrepancies: The source is a six-panel static composition labeled (a)-(f) showing successive MAX-HEAPIFY states; the generated default view shows only the initial single tree with no shaded node, and the (a)-(f) panel identifiers are absent (the states exist only as playback frames/captions).

In source panel (a) the current node i=5 (value 16) is filled dark gray with an italic 'i' beside it; the generated step-0 frame shows no shaded node and no italic 'i', so the default does not read like the source's first panel.
The source array bar carries no per-cell index numbers; the generated figure adds small index digits above every array cell (minor extra chrome).

A large right-hand code-editor/control panel (tabs, textarea, run button, playback, speed, log) dominates the layout and compresses the tree into the left half, unlike the source where the tree fills the panel.
Node circles and inter-node spacing are noticeably smaller/tighter than the source because the tree is squeezed beside the control panel, changing the figure's proportions at a glance.

Give the tree more horizontal space (narrow or collapse the side panel by default) and enlarge node radius/spacing so proportions match the source.
